answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and put them face down on the bottom. Shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them. Shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down Conflict Deck construction.

answers.answer: In four-player play, a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. In either case they start with two Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in their garrison plus nine troops in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score spaces; Agents; troops; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain. After Revealing, you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns and cannot take another Agent turn that phase. Reveal effects come only from cards still in hand and revealed for that Reveal, not cards already played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Reveal Turn; “Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped”; Clean Up.

answers.answer: You may play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing your Agent, and resources it grants before entry can pay the cost. The played Agent card's effects and destination effects occur after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot timing; Agent Turn.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during that turn can deploy, plus up to two troops from the garrison, for at most five deployed in this example. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops stay in the garrison. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison before any eligible deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit from supply; Combat space deployment limit.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that use does not recall the Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a post connected to the destination to bypass another player's Agent there. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy when you place an Agent to draw a card; choose it immediately after placement and before any space or played-card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both effects, though two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4, totaling 11. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength; Combat Intrigue eligibility.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again if an opponent later plays a Combat Intrigue; the window closes only after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their owners' supplies (not garrisons), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Combat; Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: In both player counts, each of the two tied for first gets the second-place reward, nobody wins the Conflict, and nobody takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game the remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties; two tied first with 4 players; 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards; a second worm does not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card are not doubled. For a doubled reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP or pay 6 spice to take it twice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; rulebook example: 3 spice for 1 VP can be paid twice.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A matching pair must be flipped face down and scores 1 VP; matching is mandatory, not optional. During Endgame, the wild battle icon may match any one of the three icon types in your supply, and the pair is flipped face down for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: winner check, mandatory pair, Endgame wild icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses that VP, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again upon returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gets the Alliance and its 1 VP; that VP is tied to holding the Alliance. Tying the holder does not take it: you must rise above the holder to transfer it (with separate FAQ transfer rules if the holder loses Influence).
answers.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence and Alliance transfer rules.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn you can spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card or split one source among multiple cards. The Row refills immediately, so you may buy a replacement card if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: timing, pooling/splitting, row replacement, discard pile.

answers.answer: At Makers, add 1 spice to each unoccupied Maker space's bonus spot; visiting a Maker space gains all bonus spice there, including accumulated spice. Maker Hooks are normally obtained at Sietch Tabr and are not spent when summoning. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin until removed. Sandworms are summoned directly to the Conflict and can never be placed in a garrison; when Wall removal has occurred, they may be summoned to any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Phase 4: Makers; Sandworms; Shield Wall; Hooks retained.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Game end and tiebreakers.

answers.answer: With standard CHOAM, shuffle the 20 contracts, reveal two face up beneath the Landsraad Council, and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium deck. Shaddam is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The ten contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix and are not used in standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: setup changes; contrasting-back contracts.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank face up. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when an Agent visits a Maker space and gains at least its specified spice amount that turn, counting all sources. Immediate completes upon taking it. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract after already sending your Agent to its required space that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold it when you send the Agent. When a contract completes, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: already visited space; completion procedure.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective. First Player is assigned to the human whose Objective shows the marker, and First Player alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns but never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns.

answers.answer: If the indicated destination is occupied, the Rival ignores it and reveals another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: it tries an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore the placement, then reveal another card either way. The Rival ignores normal space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy; Hagal deck reshuffling.

answers.answer: For three or four players, remove Objectives whose player-count marking does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and give each player one face up. The Objective with the First Player marker identifies First Player. Shaddam Corrino IV must not be used without the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Leaders and Objectives.

answers.answer: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water, or sandworms, make any convenient substitution; these supplies are not limited. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Take gained resources from the bank, not another player's supply; return payments to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: bank; resources not limited; gains and payments.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top of the Conflict Deck, resolve any qualifying control defensive bonus, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next Round Start.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Round Start; Recall.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn, space effects, the played card's Agent-box effects, and the Faction Influence advance may be carried out in any order. But entry requirements and costs must be satisfied immediately before resolving the space or played card, so Influence gained from that visit cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: effects in any order; costs and requirements before resolving effects.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can normally be paid and resolved only once per turn, even if you can afford it twice; sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory, while effects marked “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are optional. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it; a direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type that must connect to the post, only a post connected to that icon is legal.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: placement and no Spies in supply.

answers.answer: No: Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Spy use does not replace the need to play a card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use two Spies for different effects, one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ: Spies.

answers.answer: A location's controller receives its bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: Arrakeen or Spice Refinery gives its controller 1 Solari; Imperial Basin gives its controller 1 spice. Winning its named Conflict gives control, replacing the opponent's marker. When that Conflict is revealed while you already control the location, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps its first reward and Conflict card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward and nobody wins or takes the card; no other rewards are given in either a three- or four-player game.
answers.evidence: Combat ties; Three tied for first.

answers.answer: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards and third receives nothing. This is also the ordinary reward rule for two humans plus the Rival; the Rival counts as a player and may win.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: player-count ranks; Required Rival Rules: shared scoring Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolving one, put it face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ: Intrigue deck runs out.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot select an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. The Steal Intrigue icon makes each opponent with four or more Intrigues give one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Trashing; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return trashed ordinary cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it is a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow VP from acquisition remains even if that card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ: Victory.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire that card, not when later playing it. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot be carried over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed earlier. Fremen Bond may use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent; you may use the recalled Agent on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect that says gain two Influence applies both to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split across two Factions. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the specified minimum for that Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice and faction-specific icons; minimum and Alliance requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with multiple opponents, the former holder chooses which of those tied opponents receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ — Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because there is no winner. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If VP, spice, Solari, water, and garrisoned troops are all tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12 despite the printed track.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Victory.

answers.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held each contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: No. Shaddam's Sardaukar contracts are set aside and do not begin in his possession. His Sardaukar Commander ability permits choosing a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract. Emperor of the Known Universe starts immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of the Training track on his Leader; when it reaches the rightmost space, it stays there for the rest of the game. Lady Jessica starts with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ: Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2. They may reach 2 with the same Faction again after losing Influence and later regaining it; moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot / Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is a Spice Trade space with no entry cost; it always draws one card and resolves its contract icon. Without CHOAM, that icon gives 2 Solari; with CHOAM and available contracts, take a contract; if none remain, gain 2 Solari. It gives no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service is an Emperor space with no entry cost; it gains 1 Emperor Influence, counted once, and resolves the same contract-icon rule. Thus Dutiful Service automatically advances Emperor once; Accept Contract does not.
answers.evidence: Faction status of contract spaces; human contract icon table; board-space table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water, gives all bonus spice, and offers either 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water, gives all bonus spice, and offers either 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Choosing worms still collects all bonus spice. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks retained.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. One option takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. The other gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, is not a Combat space, and costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits instead gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains one and 6 Solari after anyone does; it is once per player per game. You take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader, and it is available that round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster; Rival rules: a Rival gaining Swordmaster reduces human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 3 Solari and 2+ Emperor Influence, and is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; you also recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 3 spice and 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and is not a Combat space. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access and is not a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari to recruit two troops; paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support; Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner uses Spacing Guild access, is a Combat space, costs 5 spice, gives 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics uses Fremen access, is a Combat space, costs 1 water, gives 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card. Sardaukar uses Emperor access, is not a Combat space, costs 4 spice, gives 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops. Only Heighliner and Desert Tactics allow normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing and is not Combat: draw an Intrigue; gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice and is not Combat: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, costs nothing and is not Combat: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks; three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply; two Agents in supply and a Swordmaster beside the board; three Spies and 1 water in supply; and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall, and it can win by having most VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; scoring Rival.

answers.answer: Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water together, with each unit counting as one. As soon as their total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, the Rival spends that many resources and takes the third Agent, available in the current round. It spends Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, and keeps leftovers. Only resources from Hagal effects and Conflict rewards count, subject to the stated Maker and control exceptions.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After getting Swordmaster, the Rival spends each qualifying set for 1 VP: 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water. These are separate same-resource sets; seven mixed resources do not qualify for a VP.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: each such set.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival picks the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost icon in its priority list. It gains Influence VP and Alliances like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster; influence selection; numbered icon.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card the Rival selects only the destination matching current conditions; if that destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card rather than use the other destination. Accept Contract or Shipping is selected based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies or Heighliner based on Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination cards.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troop icons recruit from supply; at Combat, newly recruited troops deploy, otherwise they go to its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus that is unmet is simply omitted and does not prevent Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and 2+ Influence bonus.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores Spy placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two Spies and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, those Scheme-recruited troops deploy too. A Place Spy card with no legal post has no placement effect, but the Rival immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues that Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival collects all accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none, it takes the base 2 or 4 spice respectively; without Hooks or when the Conflict is protected from worms, it takes base spice. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks are not consumed.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces; Sandworm restrictions.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then get their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: The Rival can gain control and control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP, and sandworm reward doubling normally. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if able to pay resources or recall the needed Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward instead gives it 2 Solari, even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat; Rival never takes contracts.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total Combat strength, announce it, and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; it can be updated as needed later in the same Reveal. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play the Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns, not when you merely reveal it. Card text can override the game's usual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects that recall a Spy without a card for a specific purpose.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon and no-card effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless the instruction specifically allows it.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: When a sandworm doubles a Conflict reward of one Influence of your choice, you may pay the reward cost a second time and choose the same or a different Faction for the second gain. A single effect granting two free-choice Influence must apply both to one Faction; it cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: The Hagal Signet Ring effect resolves the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability. The Rival follows the Rival card's printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities on its Agent turns; it does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Hagal effects.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks effect takes a token only if the Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the deck. Additionally, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one Intrigue selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller gains 1 spice; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player receives the separate visit bonus too.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin; controlled locations resolve both effects.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal a new Conflict from the top of the deck and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from prior rounds. Resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards; thus the Conflict is revealed before the hands are drawn.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. The four Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of those tracks, so no human begins holding one. The Shield Wall token is placed in its marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6.

answers.answer: The player with the First Player marker takes the first Player Turn, then play proceeds clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of the phase; in 3–4 players Player Turns ends once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise. Each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; the window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: Player Turns; Phase 3: Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The Reveal turn steps are: (1) Reveal Cards, turning remaining hand cards face up; (2) Resolve Reveal Effects, including Persuasion purchases and setting strength; (3) Clean Up, moving all cards in front of you to discard. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's ten-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards; shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately and place both face down, then deal five face up to form the Imperium Row. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human's Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers start in that player's supply; the four Influence cubes start at track bottoms.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, Persuasion may acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Each card's cost is shown at its top right.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional; the player may decline even if a legal placement or recall exists. The Shield Wall detonation icon allows you to remove the token, so it is optional; once removed, it cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: ordinary placement/recall optional; Shield Wall.

answers.answer: Ordinarily the played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's access icon. A connected Spy does not give a card with only City access permission to visit Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon and you have a Spy at a post connected to Shipping, you may send the Agent there without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn, you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement can pay the destination entry cost. Resources from the card used to send the Agent or from the destination itself occur after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot timing and entry cost.

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans Reveal, Player Turns continue for the Rival's remaining Agent turns. The Rival keeps taking Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply, and never takes a Reveal turn; Combat starts once both humans Revealed and the Rival used all its Agents.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: two-player play.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit; the bonus is optional. After Conflict rewards and cleanup, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start defensive bonus; Critical Locations & Control; Phase 3 cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space; resolve the played card's Agent box. You do not reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; you place an Agent from your Leader. Spies and Infiltrate may address occupancy as separately described, but do not change the ordinary card/Agent source rules.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Clean Up; Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: The restriction takes effect immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent; he cannot delay it by choosing to resolve the board-space effects first.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Shaddam Corrino IV.

answers.answer: In a four-player Conflict with four distinct positive strengths, first, second, and third place each receive their printed reward; fourth place receives no reward. The player with highest strength wins and takes the Conflict card face up into their supply, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player rewards and winner's card procedure.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: “choose, or select at random.”

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: Maker Hooks tokens.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes a participant's deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust that player's Combat marker when the card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Use the adjusted strength on the track to resolve Combat rewards; Reveal strength is not fixed through the round.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, or water tokens come from the bank, not another player's supply. Payments are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: gains from bank and payments returned to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down first, then flip two face up for the board offers; put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. The summary does not specify a player-selected offer or preset ordering; the described procedure uses a shuffle.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: “Shuffle the 20 contracts face down, then flip two face up.”
